title: PBC implies injective acyclicity
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If $\mathrm{PBC}(f)$ holds for torsion abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-property], then $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ holds for every prime $r$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-injective-acyclicity-property]. Explicitly, after any cartesian base change [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], the higher direct images $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$ vanish for $q>0$ for every injective sheaf $I$ of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $X_{\Et}$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives), proof of (1) => (2); source Lean docstring BaseChangeProperty.lean lines 198-205

proof.text: Fix a prime $r$, a morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, a cartesian square with maps $f'$ and $g'$, and an injective $\mathbf F_r$-module sheaf $I$ on $X_{\Et}$. Its underlying abelian sheaf is torsion (it is killed by $r$), so the PBC hypothesis applies to the complex concentrated in degree $0$ with value $I$. The resulting specified derived exchange morphism is an isomorphism $g^{-1}Rf_*I\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}I$.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2), first sentence: apply the base-change hypothesis to the injective sheaf in degree zero

proof.text: The module-injective direct-image acyclicity lemma, applied to the morphism $f$ and $I$, gives $R^qf_*I=0$ for every $q>0$ (where these are the cohomology sheaves of $Rf_*I$). Thus the positive-degree cohomology of the source $Rf_*I$ is zero; its degree-zero cohomology is the ordinary direct image, by the degree-zero computation for a left exact functor and an injective resolution.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): the source has no homology outside degree zero because the injective sheaf is acyclic

proof.text: The inverse-image functor $g^{-1}$ on abelian etale sheaves is exact. On $\Dplus$ the inverse image $g^{-1}$ is computed by applying $g^{-1}$ termwise to a representing bounded below complex, and $\mathcal H^q$ of an object of $\Dplus$ is the cohomology of any representing complex. Exact functors commute with the cohomology of complexes, so for $q>0$ we have $H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*I)\cong g^{-1}H^q(Rf_*I)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): exact inverse image preserves the concentration in degree zero

proof.text: Apply the cohomology functor $H^q$ to the exchange isomorphism from Step 1. For every $q>0$ its source is zero by Step 3, hence its target $H^q(Rf'_*g'^{-1}I)$ is zero as well, since an isomorphism carries a zero object to a zero object. Here $g'^{-1}$ of the complex $I$ in degree $0$ is represented by the sheaf $g'^{-1}I$ in degree $0$ (termwise inverse image), so by the definition of higher direct image this target is $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I$.

source.place: Tag 0A4B (Lemma 59.91.6), proof of (1) => (2): transfer the vanishing across the base-change isomorphism

proof.text: The square, the prime $r$, and the injective $I$ were arbitrary. Therefore the vanishing in Step 4 is precisely $\mathrm{IA}_r(f)$ for this prime, and varying $r$ gives $\mathrm{IA}(f)$ as required.

split_report.summary: Split the PBC-to-IA direction into five steps: specialize PBC to an injective prime-field module sheaf in degree zero, use module-injective direct-image acyclicity and the degree-zero derived identification, transport vanishing through exact inverse image and cohomology, transfer it across the exchange isomorphism, and conclude the quantified IA property. The source's sorry-free theorem is module-valued for arbitrary coefficients and was checked but retained as a related declaration rather than an exact attachment.
